note: Scripted egocentric streams for Vinci. Each stream is a sequence of moments seen through the head-mounted camera. At every moment the backend calls the inference service in silent mode with four frames, written here as text, and the model's one-line description is stored with its timestamp. At the end the user says the wake word and asks questions while looking at the current scene. 'time' is seconds since the session started; the adapter sets the service clock to it. 'design' records why the stream was chosen and is never sent to a model.

streams.setting: A weekday morning at home before leaving for work.
streams.design: The keys go to an unusual place at 24 s and the pill is taken at 48 s; at question time the camera shows only the empty key hook and the door, so both answers need the stored history.

My hand lets go of the mug; the coffee machine's display shows 'READY'.

My right hand holds a set of car keys with a red leather tag.
I turn toward the kitchen island, where a wooden fruit bowl holds three apples and a banana.

The keys lie in the fruit bowl; the red tag hangs over the rim.

Water soaks into the soil of the basil pot.
I set the watering can down next to the sink.
Raindrops run down the window glass.
A seven-day pill organiser on the counter, lids labelled MON to SUN.
My thumb flips open the lid marked TUE; one small blue pill is inside.
I tip the blue pill into my palm.
I swallow the pill with a glass of water.
The fridge door is open; my hand takes a carton of oat milk from the door shelf.
I pour oat milk into the white mug of coffee.
I put the carton back on the fridge door shelf.
The fridge door swings shut.
I walk down a narrow hallway holding the mug.
A navy raincoat hangs on a hook; I take it down.
My arms go into the raincoat sleeves.
I zip the raincoat up to the chest.
The front door with a small row of hooks beside it; the hook labelled KEYS is empty.
My hand pats the raincoat pockets.

My hand rests on the door handle.
The front door and the empty KEYS hook beside it.
My hand pats the raincoat pockets again.

The hallway light is on.
questions.question: Where did I leave my car keys?
questions.answer: In the wooden fruit bowl on the kitchen island, among the apples (at about 24 s).

frames: The front door, seen from close up.
My hand holds the door handle.
I glance at my wristwatch showing 08:12.
Rain is visible through the door's small window.
questions.question: Did I take my pill this morning?
questions.answer: Yes. At about 48 s I took the blue pill from the TUE compartment of the pill organiser and swallowed it with water.

streams.setting: Cooking dinner alone in a small kitchen, with an interruption at the door.
streams.design: The salt goes in at 20 s and the timer is set at 40 s; after the parcel delivery at 60-70 s the pot alone does not show whether it was salted, so both answers need the stored history.

The stove has four gas burners; all are off.
I set the pot on the back-left burner.
My hand turns the back-left knob; a blue flame appears.
I turn the knob to the highest setting.
Small bubbles start to form at the bottom of the pot.
My hand takes a red box of coarse sea salt from the shelf above the stove.
I scoop one heaped tablespoon of salt out of the box.
I tip the tablespoon of salt into the pot of water.
I put the red salt box back on the shelf above the stove.

I chop the garlic finely.
I push the chopped garlic to the side of the board.
The water in the pot is boiling hard.
I drop a handful of spaghetti into the pot.
My phone in my hand shows a timer set to 9:00.
I tap Start; the timer shows 8:59.
I stir the spaghetti with a wooden spoon.
The spaghetti softens and sinks under the water.
Steam rises from the pot.
I lean the wooden spoon on the edge of the pot.
I walk out of the kitchen toward the front door.
I open the door; a courier holds a small cardboard parcel.
I sign on the courier's handheld screen.
I take the parcel and close the door.
Back in the kitchen, I put the parcel on the table.
The pot is still boiling on the back-left burner.
My phone on the counter shows the timer at 6:51.
I look at the red salt box on the shelf above the stove.
The boiling pot of spaghetti on the back-left burner.
The red salt box on the shelf above the stove.
My hand hovers over the salt box.
The phone timer on the counter shows 6:43.
questions.question: Did I already salt the pasta water?
questions.answer: Yes. At about 20 s one heaped tablespoon of coarse sea salt from the red box went into the water, before the pasta.

frames: The pot of spaghetti, boiling.
The parcel on the kitchen table.
The phone on the counter, screen dark.
My hand reaches for the wooden spoon.
questions.question: How long did I set the pasta timer for?
questions.answer: Nine minutes, started at about 40 s when the spaghetti went in.

streams.setting: A weekly shop at a supermarket with a list on the phone.
streams.design: The list is shown at 45 s and the items are picked at different moments; the question at the checkout asks what is still missing, and a second question asks for a detail read earlier.

questions.answer: Yes, the basil. Lemons, oat milk, eggs and dish soap are in the basket.

streams.setting: An afternoon at an office desk.
streams.design: The calendar entry is visible at 0 s, the USB drive goes into the drawer at 12 s; at question time the user is at the printer, so both answers need the stored history.
